# [TASK] CI/CD: container image publish + gated deploy workflows

## Task
Build CI/CD workflows to publish container images and let deploys be triggered on demand (ARCHITECTURE.md §11.4): `docker-publish.yml` builds and pushes all backend service images to ghcr.io after Backend CI goes green on `main`; `deploy.yml` is a manual `workflow_dispatch` (`azure` or `aws`) that runs `kubectl apply -k overlays/<cloud>` — no automatic deploy on merge, to protect free-tier hours.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `docker-publish.yml` triggers only via `workflow_run` after Backend CI succeeds on `main`, matrixes over all 7 services, pushes `:latest` + `:<git-sha>` tags
- [x] `deploy.yml` is manual-dispatch-only, no auto-trigger
- [x] All 7 service images build and push on a green Backend CI run — verified 2026-08-01 (commit `2516f31`); the `ai-service` protobuf/Alpine build bug found along the way was fixed (build stage moved off Alpine to glibc)
- [x] `deploy.yml` verified against both Azure and AWS targets — OIDC auth, repo variables/secrets, Terraform state reads, and guardrails confirmed working for both (2026-08-01)
- [x] ghcr.io packages are public — true by default for packages the workflow creates itself; confirmed on all 7

## Estimate
**Hours:** 8

## Notes
If a package is manually pushed to ghcr.io with a personal token before the workflow first runs, the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't write to it afterward (not repo-linked) — delete the package and let the workflow create it fresh.

Reference: ARCHITECTURE.md §11.4
